static_traits.name: Zhou Li
static_traits.social_status: Having a close friend living nearby, but not yet discussing current troubles with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; no prior psychotherapy/counseling history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic; anxious emotional tone; able to describe vivid imagery and trigger situations concretely; skeptical about change but willing to try, fair cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: Since falling while hiking once, I have felt strong fear and anxiety about tripping while out and breaking my ankle again, appearing almost every time I go for a walk or hike, causing marked distress and avoidance.
basic_info.core_demands: Because fear and anxiety have started interfering with daily life and enjoyment of outdoor activities, making it hard to walk or hike, I decided to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: A fall while hiking once, accompanied by physical pain and a strong embarrassing experience. Afterwards gradually developing persistent fear and anxiety about 'tripping again while out and breaking the ankle'; vivid images of falling again surface in mind whenever thinking of walking or hiking, symptoms worsening over time; reducing or even avoiding outdoor activities to avoid risk, and constantly checking surroundings when having to go out.

core_beliefs: The external environment is full of danger; accidents can happen at any time
I am very fragile and unsafe, unable to effectively protect myself from harm

special_situations.event: Thinking about going out for a walk (e.g., preparing to go out last week)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I go out walking, falling is almost inevitable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Simply stays home to completely avoid risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I will fall again, staying home is safer

special_situations.event: Seeing small stones or uneven places on the road
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even a slight stumble will lead to serious injury (such as a fractured ankle)
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Slowing pace, staring fixedly at the ground, only choosing routes that look extremely flat
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: One stumble will break my ankle

special_situations.event: Recalls the hiking fall experience and the pain/embarrassment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One fall means I will fall every time in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Giving up hiking and most outdoor activities, avoiding triggering similar situations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just someone who keeps falling

special_situations.event: Scanning the environment throughout when having to go out, looking for potential dangers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Dangers everywhere, must constantly watch unsafe details to barely avoid disaster
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive vigilance and continuous environmental checking, hard to enjoy walking itself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The floor is full of things that will make me have another accident

core_conflict.wish: Longing for safety and control, able to enjoy outdoor activities without worry
core_conflict.fear: Fears being hurt and losing control again, and feels shame and being evaluated by others because of accidents
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of security by avoiding going out and excessive checking
Avoiding being seen as weak or exaggerating through not disclosing and not asking for help

object_relations.self_representation: The fragile individual prone to injury and judgment
object_relations.object_representation: People who may think I am weak and exaggerating

object_relations.self_representation: Vulnerable one who must always guard against danger
object_relations.object_representation: The external world/environment is a place full of potential threats

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites exploring and challenging catastrophic thoughts and discussing possible changes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing 'talking will not change anything', change is futile
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding briefly in a low, doubtful tone, emphasizing 'no use', reducing elaboration of details.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether one is willing to share troubles with a close friend and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Presets that others will see her as weak or overreacting (others will judge me)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoiding disclosure, emphasizing 'not wanting to appear weak/overreacting', restrained tone, possibly displacing to factual description.

manifestations: After one accident, significantly contracts the choice of 'going out walking/hiking'
Countering uncertainty and risk with avoidance and excessive control
outcomes: Limited life scope; less outdoor enjoyment

manifestations: Choosing not to share and not ask for help despite having a close friend nearby
outcomes: Social support hard to take effect, increased emotional burden

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Worries about 'appearing weak / overreacting'; is especially cautious in sharing and seeking help
First expressing the doubtful attitude of 'talking is useless' in session, cautiously trying change

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Choosing not to ask for help despite having a close friend, bearing anxiety and fear alone
Handling external contact with self-repression and avoidance (going out less)

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Presupposes others will see oneself as weak or exaggerating, thus avoids disclosure
Assuming negative evaluation before social contact and withdrawing

positive_force: Has a close friend who lives nearby (a potential social support resource)
Willing to try exploring and challenging thoughts, can accept suggestions of evidence-based methods
Fairly clear self-awareness of trigger cues and vivid imagery
Once loved outdoor activities; has inner motivation to resume participation
negative_force: Significant cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, predicting the future, mental filtering
Avoiding going out and excessive checking maintaining anxiety and insecurity
Shame and self-stigma (worrying about being seen as weak) hinder help-seeking and support mobilization
Painful fall-related memories and vivid imagery frequently triggering strong fear
Pessimistic beliefs about change ('talking is useless') lowering motivation to try

antecedent: Thinking about or planning to go out for a walk / hike
Recalling the experience and images of once falling
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic/predicting-the-future beliefs and painful memories (pain and embarrassment) formed after the hiking fall reinforcing risk-assessment bias
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential danger and strong anxiety, temporarily gaining a sense of security
target_behavior.consequence: Outdoor activities markedly reduced, decreased enjoyment of life, less physical exercise, overall increased stress

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive environmental checking and high alertness when going out
antecedent: Seeing uneven road surfaces or small stones while walking outdoors
target_behavior.core_reason: Overestimation of accidental risks and an excessive need for control (generalized from one fall experience)
target_behavior.function: Seeking control and lowering uncertainty to relieve anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: The walking process tense and effortful, unable to enjoy the activity, anxiety hard to fade naturally and maintained
